title: Canonical tensor and proper/open arrows for varying coefficient systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the coefficient rings $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $W$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the actual ring $B_\bullet(n,U)=(A_{n+1})_W(U)$ on the vertical sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. The module category and its ordinary unbounded derived category are the published strict semilinear models [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Define the following universal presentation and canonical arrows; no coefficient transition is assumed flat.

For $f:X\to Y$, the structural ring map $B_{\bullet,Y}\to f_*B_{\bullet,X}$ is the unique map preserving every constant scalar at every index. Define $f_*$ by precomposition with $(1,f^\mathrm{base}):\mathbf N\times Y_\mathrm{proet}\to\mathbf N\times X_\mathrm{proet}$ and restriction along this ring map. It is additive; the system module categories admit K-injective resolutions. A universal presentation consists of the published derived tensor/Hom calculus on each actual system category, an exact additive left adjoint $f^*$ to this specified $f_*$, and an exact additive $j_!\dashv j^*$ for each open immersion. Such presentations exist. The open unit is invertible. Direct-image composition is the unique section map induced by fibre-product pasting; pullback composition is its adjunction conjugate. Derive the exact functors termwise and direct image by its total right derived functor, with the canonical derived adjunction of the ordinary adjunction.

For ordinary systems $M,N$ on $X$, the canonical lax tensor map $f_*M\otimes f_*N\to f_*(M\otimes N)$ is the unique map carrying every local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ to that same pure tensor on the pulled-back object. Require the ordinary inverse-image tensor comparison to be its adjunction transpose after the two units. The derived comparison $\mu_f:P_f(M\otimes^LN)\cong P_fM\otimes^LP_fN$ is fixed by the published TensorComparisonModel: the inverse ordinary map on every signed total-complex summand and localization on flat-term K-flat system representatives. These tensor presentations exist with the preceding ordinary operations.

For a commutative square with top $k:A\hookrightarrow B$ and bottom $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ quasi-compact open, left $r:A\to C$ and right $p:B\to D$ proper, let $\theta:k^*p^*\cong r^*i^*$ be the canonical composition comparison. Define the ordinary map $a:p^*i_!\to k_!r^*$ as the unique natural transformation satisfying
$$k^*(a_N)=u_{k,r^*N}\circ r^*(u_{i,N}^{-1})\circ\theta_{i_!N}.$$
This unique map exists and is the open-base-change composite followed by the identity/zero component projection for the clopen lift $s:A\to B\times_D C$ of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Localize this actual ordinary transformation on complexes. Define $\gamma:i_!R_r\to R_pk_!$ to be its proper-adjunction mate. For arbitrary unbounded systems define $\pi_{f;M,N}$ as the transpose of $\mu_f$ followed by $\varepsilon_{f,M}\otimes1$. Define $\delta_{j;M,N}^{-1}$ as the $j_!\dashv P_j$ transpose of $u_{j,M}\otimes1$ followed by $\mu_j^{-1}$. This specified map is invertible, by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]; $\delta_j$ is its inverse. All of these are actual morphisms in the ordinary derived categories of systems before evaluation.

proof.text: For base_continuous, apply the existing varying-ring baseChange_continuous theorem. Its sequence-site functor is definitionally the same product of the identity index functor and pro-etale base change; no coefficient transition flatness is used.

For coefficient_existsUnique, assemble the natural constant-section direct-image maps at every quotient into a natural transformation of coefficient sequences, then uncurry it. For uniqueness restrict to a quotient slice and apply the constant-presheaf sheafification adjunction: agreement on all constant scalars implies equality.
The specified direct functor is the module-sheaf pushforward. Its section maps preserve addition, so the Mathlib additive pushforward instance proves direct_additive.
Apply the independent-universe Grothendieck and functorial K-injective resolution theorem to the actual coefficient ring on the sequence site. Its resolution clause gives system_kInjective.

For laxTensor_existsUnique, compose the presheaf pushforward lax tensor map with the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor comparison, and extend through the module-sheafification adjunction. Its unit equation and the presheaf pure-tensor formula give the required section normalization. Cancel the tensor/sheafification isomorphism, use adjunction injectivity, and use tensor induction on each presheaf section to prove uniqueness. The independent-coefficient monoidal localization theorem provides the tensor/sheafification comparison at the stated universes.

For directComp_existsUnique, use the canonical fibre-product pasting isomorphism of the base-change functors. Constant-scalar preservation identifies the composite coefficient map with the structural coefficient map. This yields the sectionwise module pushforward comparison. The prescribed section formula determines all components and hence proves uniqueness.

For Operations.ordinaryOpenUnit_isIso, identify direct with the varying-ring pushforward by its constant-section normalization. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the supplied pullback with varying-ring pullback, and then identifies the supplied extension with varying-ring extension. Whisker these isomorphisms and compose with the inverse of moduleJAdj_unit_isIso to identify the supplied extension/pullback composite with the identity. Adjunction.isIso_unit_of_iso proves invertibility of the supplied unit. This replaces the duplicate sectionwise open-site construction and does not assume tensor-operation existence.

Construct the ordinary package from semilinearDerivedSections and the canonical varying-ring pullback and open extension, transporting its adjunction along direct_eq_varying. For every map apply the normalized tensor-comparison theorem on the actual tower. The equality between the two direct-image presentations transports sections by casts between definitionally equal carriers; proof irrelevance reduces these casts to the identity. Thus laxTensor_existsUnique supplies exactly the pure-tensor normalization hypothesis. Choose the per-map universal comparisons and assemble TensorOperations.

For Operations.alpha_existsUnique, first identify the specified direct-image functor with VaryingRing.push for the actual rings ULift(A_(n+1)) and their quotient maps. The equality follows from coefficient_existsUnique and the sheafification adjunction unit equation. In the pullback V = B times_F C, write v : V -> B, t : V -> C and s = (k,r) : A -> V. The lift s is clopen. The varying-ring moduleBeta and moduleJComp identify the source p^*(i_!N) and target k_!M as v_!(t^*N) and v_!(s_!M). For v_! adjoint to v^*, the counit is invertible at the source, so v^* is bijective on this Hom set. For clopen s, moduleOpenToP identifies s_! with the fully faithful s_*, and hence the unit of s^* adjoint to s_* is invertible at the target. Thus s^* is also bijective on the relevant Hom set. Pullback composition gives bijectivity of k^*. Transport this bijectivity to the supplied universal adjoints using leftAdjointUniq; naturality of the functor isomorphisms identifies the transported Hom map with the actual supplied pullback map. Assemble the prescribed square/inverse-open-unit/open-unit word q as a natural transformation. For each N take its unique preimage under k^* on Hom. Injectivity and naturality of q prove naturality of these preimages, and injectivity again proves uniqueness of the resulting transformation. All comparisons and bijections are ordinary module-system comparisons; neither derived evaluation nor tensor-operation existence is used.

Descend the inverse ordinary extension/restriction unit to an isomorphism of their derived composite with the identity; Adjunction.isIso_unit_of_iso makes the actual derived unit invertible. Compare the supplied ordinary pullback and extension with canonical varying-ring adjoints, then derive their natural isomorphism. Transport the ambient tensor support theorem along that extension comparison. Full faithfulness makes the derived counit invertible at the supported tensor target. Expand the specified adjunction transpose as extension applied to its adjunct followed by that counit. The adjunct is invertible because it is tensor of the invertible unit with the identity, followed by mu inverse. The whole composite is therefore invertible.
